key_insight: A quadrature-aware complex-linear operator learns the boundary-to-field map for acoustics while enforcing exact linear superposition over distributed surface excitation.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, physically consistent surrogate prediction of resonant acoustic pressure fields from vibrating boundaries, reducing the need for repeated wave simulations.
method: Complex-linear boundary operator (CLBO) maps complex normal velocity on a vibrating surface to complex pressure at receivers.
Uses learned source and receiver basis functions plus explicit complex surface quadrature, so source inputs are handled by coordinates, normals, and weights rather than a flattened vector.
Compared against a fixed-sensor complex DeepONet under matched splits and settings, with tests for interpolation, discretization, holdout, label efficiency, and unseen mixtures.
evidence_signal: Across five seeds, CLBO reduced mean complex relative field error to 0.184 ± 0.00771 versus 0.367 ± 0.00742 for DeepONet, with superposition error 1.31 × 10^-7 and 1.83 × 10^4× faster inference than the reference solver at the reported query size.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate surface quadrature and boundary discretization, so coarse or inconsistent geometry sampling may degrade the linear-physics benefits.
paper_title: Quadrature-Aware Complex-Linear Neural Operator for Boundary-to-Field Prediction in Resonant Acoustics
